acts.name: Where the evidence starts
acts.desc: The crucifixion, the earliest creed, and the oldest copies of the New Testament

acts.name: The objections you'll hear
acts.desc: The arguments from Hume onward that still frame every conversation about God

acts.name: What turned up later
acts.desc: Scrolls, stones and measurements that answered objections — plus the arguments still open

turningPoints.AD 30/33: Even skeptical historians treat the crucifixion as one of the most certain facts of antiquity
turningPoints.c. AD 35: A fixed creed puts resurrection belief within about five years, leaving no room for legend
turningPoints.1748: Hume argued no testimony could ever establish a miracle, and the objection has never left
turningPoints.1947: A thousand-year copying test was passed, and Isaiah 53 was proved to predate Jesus
turningPoints.1993: A hostile king's inscription named the House of David that minimalists had called a fiction
turningPoints.1998: Dark energy measured at one part in 10^120 of its natural value sharpened every fine-tuning argument
